newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: China's U.N. envoy visits countries with Taiwan ties.
newsitem.headline: China's U.N. envoy visits countries with Taiwan ties.

text.p: China's U.N. representative, ambassador Qin Huasun, recently visited Saint Kitts and Nevis, and Costa Rica, two countries which have diplomatic relations with Taiwan, a Chinese spokesman said on Wednesday.
Both countries have also been associated in the past with efforts at the United Nations to secure U.N. membership for Taipei, which was expelled from the world body in 1971 and replaced by Beijing.

The spokesman of China's U.N. mission, Chen Ranfeng, said Qin visited Saint Kitts and Nevis on April 14-15, accompanied by a number of Chinese businessmen, at the inivitation of the government of that tiny Caribbean island nation. He visited Costa Rica, also at government invitation, about three weeks earlier.

Asked whether the visits were likely to result in any change in those countries' policies toward China, Chen would say only that they would "deepen mutual understanding and be conducive to the future development of bilateral relations."

Last September, for the fourth year in a row, China defeated a bid by a group of mostly Caribbean, Central American and African countries to get the U.N. General Assembly to discuss the question of U.N. membership for Taiwan, which Beijing regards as a renegade province.
The sponsors of the move have been accused by China of succumbing to "dollar diplomacy" -- inducements in the form of Taiwanese aid and other economic benefits.
Saint Kitts and Nevis and Costa Rica were not among the sponsors of last year's bid to seat Taiwan but played a role in previous years.

Beijing feels so strongly about the Taiwan issue that in January it used its veto for the first time in nearly 25 years to block a Security Council resolution to send military observers to monitor a peace accord in Guatemala because of that country's links with Taiwan.
Two weeks later China switched signals and voted for a similar resolution, sparking speculation that Guatemala might have agreed to refrain from sponsoring any future pro-Taiwanese move.
